thread:
incident-bot: P0 detected: sudden cross-region traffic skew 4/6 nodes in eu-west-1 reporting 5xx+connect errors, spike in latency for eu customers, possible routing policy mismatch. Auto-escalate to #incidents and paging list.

oncall-pager: paging alex kim (primary oncall) and maria ramos (secondary). Please acknowledge. Pager details: https://pd.example/incident/1991234567

alex kim: acked. jumping in. initial ask: snapshot of routing policy versions + recent deploys?

maria ramos: I saw a routing policy change 23m ago by infra-automation-bot: 
```
apply routing-policy cross-region: {priority: latency, ttl: 86400, pinning: disabled}
```
then a manual rollback 7m ago to version v12 by jonas.peterson. Not sure TTL was changed on rollback.

jonas peterson: I rolled back because the new kernel was causing tail latency. I did not touch TTL explicitly, CLI said revert to v11.

alex kim: can we confirm what TTL is being served at DNS layer vs what policy setting is? I'm seeing a lot of stale caches pointing to us-east-1.

infra-automation-bot: query output: 
```
> rpolicyctl get cross-region --json
{"version":"v11","priority":"latency","dns_ttl":86400,"pinned_region":null}
```
Edge DNS returned TTL 86400 according to control plane, but authoritative zone shows TTL 30 for the routing RRset.

maria ramos: that mismatch is the red flag. Cloud DNS zone was not updated during the rollback. looks like someone patched zone to 30s earlier for canary but rollback didn't restore to 86400. caches diverging: some resolvers still using 86400 (routing decisions still long-lived), others using 30s -> flapping and asymmetry.

sre-lead: impact assessment? are any customers fully affected? we need to know scope and severity.

support-ops: initial reports from 5 accounts in EU: intermittent 5xx and elevated tail latency. No data ingestion loss reported. Estimated affected request rate: ~12% of EU traffic, error rate up to 6%. Several customers have opened tickets.

alex kim: mitigation plan: 1) reduce control-plane TTL to 60s so caches converge quickly 2) pin routing for EU customers to eu-west-1 as temporary fallback 3) monitor error rate and rollback pins after convergence.

jonas peterson: I can push a quick TTL sync to authoritative zone. will run: 
```
# set authoritative zone TTL to 60
gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-routing
gcloud dns record-sets transaction remove --name="api.redwood.ai." --ttl=86400 --type=A --zone=redwood-routing
gcloud dns record-sets transaction add --name="api.redwood.ai." --ttl=60 --type=A "<api-anycast-ip>"
gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-routing
```
Doing it now.

infra-automation-bot: executed transaction at control plane. propagation to authoritative should start.

maria ramos: starting a temporary region pin for eu requests: 
```
rpolicyctl patch cross-region --set pinned_region=eu-west-1 --ttl-sync=60 --note="temp pin during TTL converg"
```
Applying canary to 5% first.

alex kim: increase to 50% if metrics show error drop and no regression. Watch for increased load on eu-west-1.

(5m passes)

support-ops: error rate in EU down from 6% to 1.2% after canary pin. latency p95 also improved ~200ms. Customers reporting fewer errors.

jonas peterson: authoritative zone shows TTL=60 now. Verified with dig from multiple regions: TTL 60 returned.

alex kim: scaling eu-west-1 pool by +20% to absorb pinned traffic: `kube-scale --pool=eu-infer --replicas=+6`

infra-automation-bot: scaling job started, pods coming up.

sre-lead: good. next steps: keep pin for 1 hour to let caches and edge CDNs converge, then gradually revert pin and set consistent TTL back to desired final value. Also add a short postmortem note.

maria ramos: creating incident timeline and customer impact note for support: 
- root cause: rollback of routing policy version that did not update authoritative DNS TTL, creating a TTL mismatch between control plane and DNS zone following earlier low-TTL canary patch.
- mitigation: synchronized TTL to 60s, pinned eu traffic to eu-west-1 temporarily, scaled capacity.
- customer impact: ~12% EU requests, up to 6% errors at peak for 40 minutes, reduced to <1.5% after mitigation.

support-ops: I'm sending an outbound to affected customers now, linking status page and ETA.

alex kim: after 1h of stable metrics we will start unpin in 10% increments and set authoritative TTL back to 3600. Timeline:
- T+60m: begin unpin to 80%
- T+90m: unpin to 40%
- T+120m: remove pin and set TTL 3600

jonas peterson: noted. will attach deploy logs and the rollback command to the postmortem.

(1h passes)

support-ops: metrics stable. proceeding with unpin canary to 80%.

maria ramos: unpin to 80% completed, no regressions.

alex kim: proceed to 40%.

(30m)

support-ops: all checks green. initiating final unpin and TTL bump to 3600.

jonas peterson: final DNS transaction executed to set TTL=3600. rpolicyctl patch remove pinned_region.

infra-automation-bot: policy now shows pinned_region=null, dns_ttl=3600.

sre-lead: incident classified as Sev2->P1 (brief P0 but mitigated quickly). Action items: 
- automation: add guardrail to rollback operations to sync DNS zone TTL with control plane (todo: infra-automation-bot change)
- runbook: add explicit TTL check step to cross-region policy rollouts
- postmortem: owner jonas.peterson, write within 72h, include customer timeline and suggested SLA credits if needed.

alex kim: handing off to maria for postmortem writeup and support follow-ups. I'll update oncall handover doc.

maria ramos: taking ownership. creating doc: https://confluence/redwood/incidents/1991234567

support-ops: outbound sent to affected customers with timeline and mitigation details.

alex kim: closing monitoring alert. marking incident resolved in PD. Great teamwork :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident 1991234567 moved to resolved state by alex kim at T+2h.

jonas peterson: note for postmortem: consider setting default DNS TTL to match policy TTL in our IaC templates to avoid manual mismatches.

maria ramos: will include that and the automation ticket in the action items.

support-ops: I'll follow up with customers tomorrow to ensure no residual issues.

(End of thread)
